# package cia402

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-canopen/cia402"
```

Package cia402 implements the CiA 402 drive profile (IEC 61800-7-201): the power drive state machine, the modes of operation and the common 0x6xxx objects, a device-side drive model and a master-side controller.

#### Profile {#hdr-Profile}

[State](#type-state) and [DecodeStatusword](#func-decodestatusword) read the statusword (0x6041) with the CiA 402 patterns; [Command](#type-command) encodes the device control commands into the controlword (0x6040) and [DecodeControlword](#func-decodecontrolword) decodes them. [Next](#func-next) is the state diagram (transitions 0..16, also listed by [Transitions](#func-transitions)) and [Path](#func-path) the shortest command sequence between two states. [Mode](#type-mode) names the modes of operation (0x6060/0x6061) and their bits in the supported drive modes (0x6502). [Objects](#func-objects) and [AddObjects](#func-addobjects) define the common objects with their data types, access rights and PDO mappability.

#### Device side {#hdr-Device_side}

[Drive](#type-drive) is a CiA 402 device model on an [od.Dictionary](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen/od#Dictionary). Controlword and mode writes, by SDO or RPDO (remote dictionary writes) or by the application (local writes), drive its state machine; refused writes are answered with SDO abort codes. A deterministic simulation advanced by [Drive.Step](#func-drive-step) moves a virtual axis in profile position (trapezoidal profile, set-point handshake), profile velocity, profile torque, homing and the cyclic synchronous modes, and implements quick stop, halt and fault reactions per their option codes. [Drive.InjectFault](#func-drive-injectfault) simulates a fault and reports it through [DriveConfig.OnError](#func-driveconfig-onerror), where a node emits its EMCY message.

#### Master side {#hdr-Master_side}

[Controller](#type-controller) operates a remote drive through any [SDO](#type-sdo) client (the sdo package's client through [SDOFuncs](#type-sdofuncs)): [Controller.Enable](#func-controller-enable) walks the state diagram step by step, verifying each state through the statusword, and resets a fault when [ControllerOptions.ResetFault](#func-controlleroptions-resetfault) allows it; [Controller.MoveTo](#func-controller-moveto) performs profile position moves with the set-point handshake; [Controller.SetVelocity](#func-controller-setvelocity), [Controller.SetTorque](#func-controller-settorque) and [Controller.Home](#func-controller-home) cover PV, PT and HM. Failures are [\*Error](#type-error) values carrying the state reached and the fault code. The statusword is polled by SDO unless a [StatusSource](#type-statussource) (e.g. fed by a TPDO) provides it.

## Constants

```go
const (
	TorqueGain         = 100.0 // increments/s² per thousandth of rated torque
	TorqueTimeConstant = 0.1   // seconds
)
```

Torque model of the simulated load (PT, CST): an inertia with viscous friction, dv/dt = TorqueGain·torque − v/TorqueTimeConstant, so a constant torque t settles at the velocity TorqueGain·TorqueTimeConstant·t.

```go
	CtrlHomingStart          uint16 = CtrlOMS4 // HM: rising edge starts, falling edge interrupts homing
```

```go
	ErrFault = errors.New("cia402: drive fault")
	// ErrNotEnabled reports a motion command for a drive that is not (or no

	ErrNotEnabled = errors.New("cia402: operation not enabled")
	// ErrHoming reports a homing error (statusword bit 13 in HM).
	ErrHoming = errors.New("cia402: homing error")
	// ErrUnreachable reports a state that cannot be reached by commands.
```


AddObjects adds the objects of [Objects](#func-objects) to a dictionary. Objects the dictionary already has are left as they are, so an application can define some of them itself (other limits, defaults or mappability) first.

### func Objects

```go

```

Objects returns the common CiA 402 objects with their CiA 402 data types, access rights and PDO mappability. supported is the value of 0x6502 (see [SupportedModes](#func-supportedmodes)).

### func StateBits

```go
func StateBits(s State) uint16
```

StateBits returns the statusword bits 0..6 that report a state: the value of its pattern, with bit 5 (quick stop) set where the pattern leaves it open, and bit 4 (voltage enabled) set in the states with the power stage on. Unknown returns 0.

### func SupportedModes

```go

```

SupportedModes encodes modes as an 0x6502 value; modes without a bit are ignored.

### func ValidTransition

```go
func ValidTransition(n int, from, to State) bool
```

ValidTransition reports whether the state diagram has transition n from one state to another (for transition 13, from any state but Fault reaction active and Fault).

## Types

### type Command

```go
type Command uint8
```

Command is a device control command, encoded in bits 0..3 and 7 of the controlword.

Some commands share an encoding: SwitchOn and DisableOperation are both 0bxxxx\_0111, SwitchOnAndEnable and EnableOperation both 0bxxxx\_1111. Which one a controlword means depends on the state; [Next](#func-next) treats each pair identically.

```go
const (
	Shutdown Command = iota + 1
	SwitchOn
	SwitchOnAndEnable
	DisableVoltage
	QuickStop
	DisableOperation
	EnableOperation
	FaultReset
)
```

Device control commands. The zero value is "no command" (an automatic transition in [Transition](#type-transition)).

#### func DecodeControlword

```go
func DecodeControlword(cw uint16) Command
```

DecodeControlword returns the command a controlword encodes. Bit 7 set decodes as FaultReset (a device acts on its rising edge only). A controlword always decodes to a command: 0bxxxx\_0111 is SwitchOn and 0bxxxx\_1111 EnableOperation (see [Command](#type-command) for the shared encodings).

#### func Path

```go
func Path(from, to State) []Command
```

Path returns the shortest command sequence from one state to another, each command one transition. Automatic transitions are taken for granted: from Not ready to switch on the path starts at Switch on disabled, from Fault reaction active at Fault. The result is empty (not nil) when from is already to, and nil when to cannot be reached by commands (Not ready to switch on, Fault reaction active, Fault, Unknown).

#### func (Command) Bits

```go
func (c Command) Bits() uint16
```

Bits returns the controlword bits 0..3 and 7 of the command; bits the command leaves open are 0.

#### func (Command) Controlword

```go
func (c Command) Controlword(base uint16) uint16
```

Controlword returns base with bits 0..3 and 7 replaced by the command; the other bits (halt, mode-specific bits) are kept. A fault reset needs a rising edge of bit 7: write base with bit 7 clear first.

#### func (Command) String

```go
func (c Command) String() string
```

String returns the CiA 402 name of the command.

### type Controller

```go
type Controller struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Controller drives a remote CiA 402 drive through its SDO server: the state machine (statusword-verified, step by step along [Path](#func-path)), modes of operation, profile position moves with the set-point handshake, profile velocity and torque, and homing. Operations may run concurrently (e.g. a QuickStop while a MoveTo waits); the controlword is written read-modify-write under a lock.

#### func (Controller) FaultReset

```go
func (c *Controller) FaultReset(ctx context.Context) error
```

FaultReset resets a fault: a rising edge of controlword bit 7, then a wait for Switch on disabled. A drive in Fault reaction active is waited for first; a drive without a fault is left alone.

#### func (Controller) Halt

```go

```

Halt sets or clears the halt bit (8) of the controlword.

#### func (Controller) Home

```go
func (c *Controller) Home(ctx context.Context, method int8, timeout time.Duration) error
```

Home runs a homing method (0x6098) in homing mode, switching to HM when needed: it starts homing with a rising edge of bit 4 and waits, at most timeout (0: the controller's Timeout), for homing attained with target reached (bits 12 and 10), failing with ErrHoming on a homing error (bit 13). The drive must be in Operation enabled.

#### func (Controller) Mode

```go
func (c *Controller) Mode(ctx context.Context) (Mode, error)
```

Mode reads the modes of operation display (0x6061).

#### func (Controller) MoveTo

```go
func (c *Controller) MoveTo(ctx context.Context, target int32, opts *MoveOptions) error
```

MoveTo moves to a target position in profile position mode (switching to PP when needed): it writes 0x607A and the profile parameters, performs the set-point handshake (bit 4 up, wait for set-point acknowledge bit 12, bit 4 down) and, with opts.Wait, waits for target reached (bit 10). The drive must be in Operation enabled. opts may be nil.

#### func (Controller) Position

```go
func (c *Controller) Position(ctx context.Context) (int32, error)
```

Position reads the position actual value (0x6064).

#### func (Controller) QuickStop

```go
func (c *Controller) QuickStop(ctx context.Context) error
```

QuickStop sends the quick stop command. From Operation enabled it waits for Quick stop active or, per the drive's quick stop option code, for Switch on disabled; from Ready to switch on and Switched on for Switch on disabled. In other states it does nothing.

### type Drive

```go
type Drive struct {

	// pending is a transition (5 or 8) delayed until the motor stopped.

	// publication of the outputs

	// removes the write hooks and the watcher

}
```

Drive is a CiA 402 device model on an object dictionary with a simple, deterministic motion simulation. Writes of the controlword (0x6040) and of the modes of operation (0x6060), remote (SDO, RPDO) or local ([od.Dictionary.Set](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen/od#Dictionary.Set)), drive the state machine; the statusword (0x6041), the modes of operation display (0x6061), the actual values (0x6062, 0x6064, 0x606C, 0x6077) and the error code (0x603F) are kept current. The other objects (targets, profile parameters, option codes) are read from the dictionary when they are used. The simulation advances with [Drive.Step](#func-drive-step) (or [Drive.Run](#func-drive-run)).

Remote writes are refused with abort codes: the controlword with [canopen.AbortLocalControl](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortLocalControl) while the drive is not under remote control and, with StrictControlword, with [canopen.AbortDeviceState](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortDeviceState); an unsupported mode, homing method or option code with [canopen.AbortInvalidValue](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortInvalidValue); a target position outside the software position limits with [canopen.AbortValueLow](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortValueLow) / [canopen.AbortValueHigh](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortValueHigh).

Behaviour of the simulation:

  - The drive starts in Not ready to switch on and takes transition 1 at the first Step.
  - Leaving Operation enabled other than by a quick stop disables the drive function: the motor stops at once. With shutdown option code 1 (0x605B) or disable operation option code 1 (0x605C) the drive first ramps down with the profile deceleration and changes state when stopped.
  - Quick stop (0x605A) and fault reaction (0x605E) ramp down with the profile deceleration (codes 1, 5) or the quick stop deceleration (2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8: current and voltage limit are modelled as the quick stop ramp); code 0 stops at once. Quick stop codes 0..4 then go to Switch on disabled, 5..8 stay in Quick stop active (transition 16 possible). The fault reaction ends in Fault once stopped, at the earliest at the next Step.
  - Halt (bit 8) ramps down per the halt option code (0x605D: 1 profile deceleration, 2..4 quick stop deceleration); releasing it resumes.
  - PP: trapezoidal profile with 0x6081/0x6083/0x6084; set-point handshake (bit 4 / bit 12) with one buffered set-point, change set immediately (bit 5), relative (bit 6, relative to the preceding target); target reached (bit 10) when stopped at the target.
  - PV: ramps to 0x60FF with 0x6083/0x6084; bit 10 velocity reached, bit 12 speed zero. PT and CST: torque actual follows 0x6071 at once, the load moves by the torque model (TorqueGain). CSP and CSV follow 0x607A / 0x60FF every Step.
  - HM: a rising edge of bit 4 starts homing, a falling edge interrupts it. Methods 35 and 37 (current position) complete at once; the others move to [DriveConfig.HomeSwitch](#func-driveconfig-homeswitch) at the homing speed 0x6099:1 with the homing acceleration 0x609A. On arrival the position becomes the home offset 0x607C. A homing speed of 0 is a homing error (bit 13).
  - Positions are clamped to the software position limits 0x607D (active when min \< max), setting internal limit active (bit 11).

A Drive is safe for concurrent use.

#### func (Drive) InjectFault

```go
func (d *Drive) InjectFault(code uint16)
```

InjectFault signals a fault with an error code (CiA 301 / CiA 402 error codes, e.g. 0x2310 over-current, 0x5441 or 0xFF00 manufacturer): 0x603F is set, OnError is called and, unless the drive is already in Fault reaction active or Fault, it takes transition 13 to Fault reaction active, then (from a Step on, once the fault reaction stopped the motor) transition 14 to Fault.

### type DriveConfig

```go
type DriveConfig struct {
	// Modes are the supported modes of operation, a subset of
	// [SimulatedModes]; nil means all of them. They are announced in 0x6502
	// when NewDrive adds that object.
	Modes []Mode
	// StrictControlword refuses (with [canopen.AbortDeviceState]) a remote
	// controlword write whose command neither keeps the present state nor
	// triggers a transition of it. By default such commands are accepted and
	// ignored, as most drives do.
	StrictControlword bool
	// HomeSwitch is the position of the simulated home switch the homing
	// methods search for.
	HomeSwitch int32
	// OnError is called with the error code when a fault occurs (see
	// [Drive.InjectFault]) and with 0 when the fault is reset, e.g. to emit
	// an EMCY message (0x5xxx, 0xFF00...) and an error reset. It runs without
	// locks held.
	OnError func(code uint16)
	// OnTransition is called after every state transition with its number;
	// it runs without locks held.
	OnTransition func(from, to State, transition int)
}
```

DriveConfig configures a [Drive](#type-drive).

String returns the abbreviation (PP, PV, CSP...), "manufacturer(-n)" for manufacturer-specific modes and "Mode(n)" for reserved values.

#### func (Mode) SupportedBit

```go
func (m Mode) SupportedBit() uint32
```

SupportedBit returns the bit of the mode in the supported drive modes object 0x6502, or 0 for modes without one (none, reserved and manufacturer-specific modes, whose bits 16..31 the manufacturer assigns).

### type MoveOptions

```go
type MoveOptions struct {
	// Relative moves relative to the preceding target position (bit 6).
	Relative bool
	// Immediate replaces an active set-point instead of queueing behind it
	// (change set immediately, bit 5).
	Immediate bool
	// Velocity, Acceleration and Deceleration are written to 0x6081, 0x6083
	// and 0x6084 when not 0.
	Velocity, Acceleration, Deceleration uint32
	// Wait waits for target reached (bit 10).
	Wait bool
	// Timeout bounds the wait for target reached; 0 means the controller's
	// Timeout.
	Timeout time.Duration
}
```

MoveOptions are the options of a profile position move.

### type SDO

```go
type SDO interface {
	Upload(ctx context.Context, index uint16, sub uint8) ([]byte, error)
	Download(ctx context.Context, index uint16, sub uint8, data []byte) error
}
```

SDO is the SDO client a [Controller](#type-controller) uses. Errors are returned unchanged inside an [\*Error](#type-error). The sdo package's client takes extra call options; wrap it with [SDOFuncs](#type-sdofuncs):

	cia402.SDOFuncs{
		UploadFunc: func(ctx context.Context, i uint16, s uint8) ([]byte, error) { return cl.Upload(ctx, i, s) },
		DownloadFunc: func(ctx context.Context, i uint16, s uint8, b []byte) error { return cl.Download(ctx, i, s, b) },
	}

### type SDOFuncs

```go
type SDOFuncs struct {
	UploadFunc   func(ctx context.Context, index uint16, sub uint8) ([]byte, error)
	DownloadFunc func(ctx context.Context, index uint16, sub uint8, data []byte) error
}
```

SDOFuncs adapts two functions to the [SDO](#type-sdo) interface.

#### func (SDOFuncs) Download

```go
func (f SDOFuncs) Download(ctx context.Context, index uint16, sub uint8, data []byte) error
```

Download calls DownloadFunc.

#### func (SDOFuncs) Upload

```go
func (f SDOFuncs) Upload(ctx context.Context, index uint16, sub uint8) ([]byte, error)
```

Upload calls UploadFunc.

### type State

```go
type State uint8
```

State is a state of the CiA 402 power drive state machine (IEC 61800-7-201 6.3.2).

```go
const (
	Unknown State = iota
	NotReadyToSwitchOn
	SwitchOnDisabled
	ReadyToSwitchOn
	SwitchedOn
	OperationEnabled
	QuickStopActive
	FaultReactionActive
	Fault
)
```

States of the drive. Unknown is the zero value: a statusword that matches none of the patterns, and the "Start" pseudo-state of transition 0.

#### func DecodeStatusword

```go
func DecodeStatusword(sw uint16) State
```

DecodeStatusword returns the state a statusword reports, or Unknown when it matches none of the CiA 402 patterns.

#### func Next

```go
func Next(s State, c Command) (to State, transition int, ok bool)
```

Next returns the state a command leads to from a state, and the number of the transition. ok is false when the command triggers no transition in that state (the drive stays where it is). SwitchOnAndEnable from Ready to switch on returns transition 3 to Switched on; a device then continues with transition 4. Transition 16 (Quick stop active → Operation enabled) is returned as the diagram allows it, though a device takes it only with a quick stop option code 5..8.

#### func (State) String

```go
func (s State) String() string
```

String returns the CiA 402 name of the state.

### type StatusSource

```go
type StatusSource interface {
	// WaitStatusword blocks until cond reports true for a statusword (the
	// latest known one or a new one), or ctx ends. It returns the last
	// statusword seen; on ctx's end with ctx's error.
	WaitStatusword(ctx context.Context, cond func(sw uint16) bool) (uint16, error)
}
```

StatusSource delivers the statusword of the drive. The default polls 0x6041 by SDO; a source fed by a TPDO listener reacts faster and spares the bus.

### type Transition

```go
type Transition struct {
	// Number is the transition number, 0..16.
	Number int
	// From is the state left; Unknown for transition 0 (from Start) and
	// transition 13 (from any state).
	From, To State
	// Command triggers the transition; 0 for transitions the drive takes by
	// itself (0, 1, 13, 14, and 12 after a completed quick stop).
	Command Command
}
```

Transition is one transition of the CiA 402 state diagram.

#### func Transitions

```go
func Transitions() []Transition
```

Transitions returns the CiA 402 state diagram: every transition with the command that triggers it (a transition triggered by two commands appears twice).
